definition: Sun Wukong went from the Stone Monkey to the Victorious Fighting Buddha through six career stages; each stage's employer, salary, rank, satisfaction, and reason for leaving reflect a career curve from 'wild outsider' to 'inside the system' and finally 'retirement from the arena'

career_stages.name: Stone Monkey King
career_stages.title: Handsome Monkey King of Flower-Fruit Mountain
career_stages.salary: No salary; 100% of Flower-Fruit Mountain's income retained; use as needed
achievements: Founded Flower-Fruit Mountain and led 47,000 monkeys
Studied under Patriarch Subhuti, gaining immortality and the 72 transformations
Forcefully crossed his name off the Ledger of Life and Death, escaping the Underworld
Borrowed treasure from the Dragon Palace, obtaining the As-you-will Gold-banded Staff (Ruyi Jingu Bang)
career_stages.leaving_reason: Yearned for a Heavenly Court post; lured into the system by Taibai Jinxing's offer of amnesty

career_stages.name: Bimawen
career_stages.title: Bimawen, Chief of the Imperial Stables
career_stages.salary: No defined salary; room and board; an 'unranked' official post
career_stages.career_level: L1 · Grassroots management; the lowest Heavenly Court post (unranked)
achievements: Raised the heavenly horses' breeding rate; horses grew plump
Completed the Court's smallest business unit (horse-keeping)
career_stages.leaving_reason: Learned that 'Bimawen' was the lowest Heavenly Court post (unranked); wounded pride; rebelled and left Heaven

career_stages.name: Great Sage Equal to Heaven
career_stages.title: Great Sage Equal to Heaven (empty title, no real power)
career_stages.salary: No salary; no real power; merely 'an office without emolument'; title only
career_stages.career_level: L2 · Honorary advisor; in name only
achievements: Obtained the empty title 'Great Sage Equal to Heaven'
Oversaw the Peach Orchard (really guarding the gate + stealing peaches)
Wrecked the Peach Banquet; stole Laozi's elixirs
Havoc in Heaven; defeated 100,000 heavenly troops and generals
career_stages.leaving_reason: Not being invited to the Peach Banquet exposed the empty title; the Jade Emperor broke his word; pinned under Five Elements Mountain by Tathāgata for 500 years

career_stages.name: Pilgrim Sun
career_stages.title: Chief disciple of Tang Sanzang; the Pilgrim
career_stages.salary: No salary; room and board (alms); stock options (the promise of Buddhahood)
achievements: Escorted Tang Sanzang 108,000 li westward to fetch the scriptures
Subdued demons over 40 times
Called in reinforcements 15 times, building a network
Completed the 81 trials and reached Vulture Peak
career_stages.leaving_reason: Project complete; pilgrimage succeeded; stock options vested (Buddhahood)

career_stages.name: Victorious Fighting Buddha
career_stages.title: Victorious Fighting Buddha
career_stages.salary: Buddhahood; incense offerings; merit accumulation; eternal honor
achievements: Completed the pilgrimage; titled Victorious Fighting Buddha
The golden headband loosened on its own; freed from restraint
Ranked among the Buddhas of Vulture Peak
Attained the right fruit; transcended samsara
career_stages.leaving_reason: No departure; merit complete; formally took his place at Vulture Peak

career_stages.name: Retirement
career_stages.title: Retired Buddha (fictional extrapolation)
career_stages.employer: No employer; free agent; roaming the four seas
career_stages.salary: Buddhahood annuity; Flower-Fruit Mountain trust income; self-sufficient
achievements: Returned to Flower-Fruit Mountain and reunited with his monkeys
Roamed the Three Realms as a free agent
Buddhahood enjoyed forever; no KPIs
Discussed the Way with the Buddhas; taught disciples

career_insights: Wukong's career curve is the standard path of 'startup – co-opted – setback – re-startup – acquired – partner – retirement'
The Bimawen affair is the Journey to the West world's 'mid-career crisis'; blocked grassroots promotion led to backlash
The Great Sage Equal to Heaven's 'office without emolument' is a trap of the Court system: pacified with a title but given no real power
The pilgrimage is a classic 'equity incentive': future options (Buddhahood) in exchange for present low-wage labor
The golden headband is a 'non-compete agreement': prevents job-hopping or rebellion, and loosens once the project ends
The title of Victorious Fighting Buddha is a 'partner promotion': from executor to shareholder
Wukong's biggest lesson: going it alone (Havoc in Heaven) failed; teamwork (the pilgrimage) succeeded
